Before · Beta 1.2 Historical

Historical source snapshot only; the shipped Beta 1.2 build was not independently verified.

Shape key: pill = start/end · rectangle = action · ◇ = decision · cylinder = stored state.

START · first use
↓
01OnboardingSix-screen historical preview · begins here
  1. Welcome.
  2. Static protected-site preview; sample only.
  3. Preview a 48-hour hold and 24-hour decision window.
  4. Preview sample savings; not evidence of an outcome.
  5. Preview Urgente as one use per month.
  6. Finish writes onboarding completion, then opens the popup.
↓
02Protected-site setupPopup list · archived code snapshot
  1. Popup reads the stored protected-site list.
  2. User adds or removes a site; the list is written to Chrome sync storage.
  3. Only a matching protected domain enters the checkout check.
↓
03Checkout interceptionArchived flow is checkout-led, not browsing-led
  1. Trigger: a checkout attempt on a protected site.
  2. Read: protected-site list and existing hold timestamp.
  3. If no active hold, write a hold start to sync storage and show the hold overlay.
  4. Decision: take the historical “Bypass Test” path, or go back and leave checkout.
  5. If not bypassed, checkout waits through the 48-hour hold.
↓
04Decision window48-hour hold → 24-hour choice window
  1. After 48 hours, show “Buy now” or “Drop it” during the 24-hour choice window.
  2. Buy now removes the site hold and allows checkout for that session.
  3. Drop it asks for confirmation, then attempts cart clearing; the archived tests expect logging only after confirmed removal.
  4. On expiry, no silent cart clear; the next checkout check starts a new hold.
↓
END · buy, drop, or return to hold

Historical source gap: onboarding says Urgente is monthly, while the clean archive code shows a typing-test bypass. Actual shipped Beta 1.2 runtime is unknown.

Plain-text fallback
First run: welcome → static protected-site preview → 48-hour hold preview → sample-savings preview → monthly Urgente preview → finish / open popup.
Shop: popup site list → protected shop → checkout attempt → read site + hold state → historical hold / bypass-test path → 48-hour hold → 24-hour Buy now or Drop it → expiry prompt; no automatic cart clearing.

After · Cognoscene v1.3 Planned target

Evidence read from current manifest 1.4.103 and source; no Git metadata or browser proof. Current v2 code informs, but does not rename, the v1.3 target.

Shape key: pill = start/end · rectangle = action · ◇ = decision · cylinder = stored state.

START · first use
↓
01Onboarding · production challengeExplicit setup is present; a production-grade redesign is plannedENHANCED

Verified currentPlanned challengeCurrent source has five screens; improving onboarding and UI remains Daniella’s challenge.

  1. Trigger: first run or a deliberate replay; read existing settings and protected sites.
  2. Show the welcome, site setup, checkout pause, evidence-first progress, and ready/privacy screens.
  3. User manually adds one or more sites; the page cannot advance with an empty selection.
  4. Optional Chrome Top Sites suggestions require a separate unchecked-by-default choice; suggestions are local and never auto-protect a site.
  5. Finish writes the selected sites, completion flag, skip flag, and settings; onboarding skip unlocks the extension without replacing the site list.
  6. Current sync-across-devices choice is prechecked by default. Consent wording/default needs review in the onboarding challenge.
↓
02Protected-site shoppingOnly user-chosen domains are eligibleENHANCED

Verified currentTop Sites suggestions are separate from the explicit protection list.

  1. Read the user’s selected domains and separate shopping-suggestion consent.
  2. If Chrome Top Sites or the shopping registry is unavailable, show no suggestions; never infer consent.
  3. Only an explicitly added domain can enter Observer, Product Pulse, or checkout eligibility.
↓
03Observer + Product PulsePaired browsing and cart-growth branchNEW

Verified currentFive-return UI incompleteSource and focused tests exist; tests were not run for this handover.

  1. Observer: on a protected site, read user frequency, active-hold state, prompt cooldown, and qualifying activity; current code requires an active-minute threshold plus fresh scrolling and a natural pause.
  2. Show a soft or active check-in only when eligible; the user may leave or continue. Continued prompts can ask a user-confirmed need; never infer motive.
  3. Write bounded prompt/answer state. The fifth-return reason has event-contract support, but the user-facing five-return prompt is missing in current source.
  4. Product Pulse: independently confirm rendered cart additions; below seven items it stays quiet.
  5. At seven or more items and outside its 60-second cooldown, show the cart-growth prompt; if it is open, defer Observer.
  6. Dismissal records the bounded pulse event; Observer may resume after a five-second delay. Uncertain DOM evidence means no pulse.
↓
04Rationalisation · checkout holdFirst qualifying checkout starts a 24-hour holdENHANCED

Verified currentMerchant proof incompleteStatic tests cover selected controls; browser support is not universal proof.

  1. Trigger only on a qualifying merchant checkout action for a protected brand; Cognoscene’s own prompt controls do not count as merchant checkout.
  2. Read brand hold, active Urgente pass, and checkout classification; uncertainty fails open.
  3. Show the hold UI and write the brand-scoped start time; ordinary browsing and add-to-cart remain available.
  4. Keep the original hold clock across reloads and matching brand subdomains; do not restart it on a return loop.
  5. At 24 hours, transition to the separate 24-hour Deliberation window; an expired window returns to a fresh hold only at a later qualifying checkout.

During the active hold · two optional routes, neither changes the timer

↶Rationator · return loopOptional pause while browsing during the holdNEW

Verified current sourceBrowser proof incompleteLocal per-tab/per-hold state only.

  1. On a neutral page during the active hold, read the hold start and return-availability state.
  2. Show the hold reminder; the user may dismiss it or choose “take a pause.”
  3. Rationator offers optional hobby/work directions or careful browsing; it does not decide or alter checkout.
  4. Choosing careful browsing records a site-and-hold key in tab session storage and returns to the persistent Rationator card.
  5. “Take a pause” reopens Rationator; dismissing the surface returns to the same active hold with its original timer.
  6. Clear the loop when the hold expires, is bypassed, or enters Deliberation.
↗Urgente · unlimited useTyped, brand-specific, checkout-only passENHANCED

Founder-confirmedVerified currentLegacy monthly counter remains

  1. Trigger from the active checkout hold; read the same-brand pass. There is no monthly usage gate.
  2. Show the optional typing challenge; user may finish it or cancel and keep the hold.
  3. On success, write a 12-hour same-brand checkout pass locally, then expose checkout for that brand only.
  4. The old monthly usage counter still increments for display/reset history; it does not limit use. Observer and Product Pulse remain separate.
  5. After 12 hours, remove the pass; the next protected checkout again reads the hold state.

Rationator loops back into the active hold. It is not a stage after the hold.

↓
05Deliberation · user choosesOpens after the 24-hour holdENHANCED

Verified current sourceNormal pass duration needs founder sign-offGrowth remains tentative and outside the active journey.

  1. Read the original brand hold, decision-window end, settled cart evidence, and any pending user choice.
  2. Show the separate 24-hour window with continue/buy, wait, and selected-item edit options; no automatic purchase.
  3. Only an explicit buy/continue confirmation may grant a temporary brand-scoped checkout permission.
  4. Selected-item changes remain on the merchant’s own cart; record a reduction only when the settled cart confirms it.
  5. Unknown price, item, or removal evidence stays unknown; do not invent a saving or claim a purchase was prevented.
  6. At expiry, remove the episode and show a brief notice that the cart is unchanged, with a “Continue browsing” action; a later qualifying checkout starts a fresh hold.
↓
END · the user keeps the decision
Growth · tentative / grey Not an active v1.3 shopper-flow stage or downloadable component until Cogno unlocks it.
REMOVED Beta 1.2’s sample-savings preview and 48-hour hold are not carried forward. The old monthly Urgente cap is not a v1.3 rule; its historical runtime remains unverified.
Plain-text fallback
First run → improved onboarding challenge → user-selected protected sites → protected-site browsing: Observer + Product Pulse.
Merchant checkout action → 24-hour Rationalisation hold. During the hold: Rationator loops back into that same hold; Urgente is an unlimited-use, 12-hour, brand-scoped checkout-only branch.
After 24 hours → 24-hour Deliberation window → explicit user choice. Growth remains tentative and outside the active v1.3 path.
